title: security: RBAC v2 enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging enhancements
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: tighten data residency guarantees and improve auditability for KMS-backed secrets in RBAC v2. This change enforces region pinning for KMS keys referenced by customer resources when org policy requires residency, and extends audit logging so every KMS bind/unbind decision is recorded with explicit policy decision metadata. The PR implements policy enforcement, a migration shim for existing bindings, console + CLI surface updates, and e2e tests. Changes are gated behind a feature flag (rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce) and rolled out progressively via a configuration toggle in Dedicated/Private.

What this PR does (high level):
- Policy: adds enforcement rule to RBAC v2 engine to validate KMS key region matches resource residency constraints. Enforcement can be audit-only or hard-enforce based on org policy.
- Audit logging: augment audit_event payloads for kms.bind and kms.unbind with policy_id, decision (allow/deny/audit), evaluated_rules, and resolved_key_region. Logs are sent to the existing audit pipeline and surfaced in Console.
- Migration: migration script that marks existing bindings as "unverified" and triggers a background verification job for orgs with residency policies; provides tooling to bulk-approve bindings per customer request.
- Console/CLI: UI strings, validation messages, and a new admin page for "KMS residency audit" showing recent decisions and remediation actions. CLI adds --verify-kms-residency command.
- Tests: unit tests for policy engine, integration tests for audit payloads, and e2e test simulating cross-region binding rejection.
- Docs: updates to security/rbac and private-deploy docs describing KMS residency behavior and migration steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Policy implementation in rbac engine
- [x] Audit event schema change and pipeline mapping
- [x] Migration shim + background verifier job
- [x] Console + CLI updates and i18n strings
- [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests added
- [x] Docs + release notes
- [x] Feature flag gating + rollout plan

Testing and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky integration test (tests/integration/kms_bind_test) failing due to timing in the background verifier. Reproduced locally and fixed by adding retry semantics and a short backoff. Full CI (unit/integration/e2e) passed after fix. Manual verification performed on a staging cluster with sample orgs: org-with-residency (expected enforcement) and org-without-residency (no change).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main with feature flag off by default.
2) Enable audit-only mode for a small set of orgs (canary) for 48h, monitor audit dashboard and error rates.
3) After no regressions, enable hard-enforce for selected customers with explicit comms.
4) Full enablement after two weeks and customer confirmations.

Backward compatibility notes: enforcement is opt-in via org policy and feature flag. Existing bindings are left in place as "unverified" and will remain functional until orgs flip to hard-enforce. Admins can use the bulk-approve tool to verify keys when appropriate.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (RBAC v2 residency enforcement), SEC-317 (audit schema for KMS events). Jira SUP-879 captures customer requests for KMS region controls.

Release notes: "Add enforcement for KMS region residency in RBAC v2 with improved audit logging. Feature is gated and requires admin review for enforcement mode. See security docs for migration steps."

release_notes: Add enforcement for KMS region residency in RBAC v2 with improved audit logging. Gated by feature flag; migration tool included.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report KMS bind failures after enabling enforcement, check feature_flag rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce, review audit events for decision=deny and evaluated_rules, and use the verifier job logs (jobs/kms_residency_verifier) to inspect failures. Migration script sets bindings to unverified; use cli cmd 'redwood kms verify --org <org_id>' to trigger verification.
security_impact: Medium — changes enforcement boundaries for KMS bindings. Default behavior remains audit-only until orgs opt into hard enforcement. Audit logging added for full decision traceability.
